channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: Queen Anne house with stained glass, historic woodwork lists in St. Paul for $775K
item.description: Built in 1891, the Victorian-era home offers 3,741 square feet and has had the same owner for the past 40 years.

item.title: New documentary ‘Under the Rainbow’ sheds fresh light on ruby slipper theft
item.description: Debuting at the Slamdance Film Festival this weekend, it features the thief who turned the global spotlight on Grand Rapids, Minn.

item.title: Fewer than 500 ICE agents remain in Minnesota, lawmakers say
item.description: U.S. Reps. Ilhan Omar and Angie Craig learned of the state of Operation Metro Surge during a visit to the Whipple Federal Building on Friday.

item.title: Girls hockey state tournament teams revel in connections to U.S. Olympians
item.description: Schools like Breck, Warroad and Dodge County can count alumni, siblings and neighbors among those playing hockey, and winning medals, at the Milan Cortina Games.

item.title: White House, Minnesota Supreme Court chief justice quietly negotiated deal over ICE enforcement in courts
item.description: Four days later, chaos unfolded inside the Hennepin County Government Center.

item.title: Minneapolis weighs two options, both heavy on affordable housing, for old Kmart site
item.description: Two developers have put forth plans for housing, nonprofit services and retail at Nicollet Avenue and Lake Street; residents are asked to weigh in.

item.title: Scoggins: USA Hockey is on the verge of a historic Olympic double
item.description: The U.S. women’s hockey team already has their gold medal win against Canada. The men’s team is up next on Sunday at the Milan Cortina Games.

item.title: Federal judge: U.S. Attorney’s Office refrain of low staffing, massive caseload ‘has worn out its welcome’
item.description: U.S. District Judge Laura Provinzino said the courts have been more than patient with prosecutors struggling to comply with court orders amid a surge of immigration cases.
